title: The stages of absorption (1.41–1.46)
hook: a clear crystal on a red cloth looks red; Patanjali says a still mind behaves the same way

segments.voice: Yesterday: mastery from the smallest to the largest, and a promise: the clear crystal. Did the tea and the sky both get your full attention? Today the crystal itself. Day four hundred forty-four.

Put a clear glass bead on a red cloth. It looks red. Slide it onto blue silk. It looks blue. Set it on a leaf, and it glows green. The bead hasn't changed at all. It has no color of its own, and that's exactly why it can show every color perfectly. Most of the time our minds aren't like that. They're tinted glass: everything we look at comes back colored with our worry, our wanting, our labels. Sutra 1.41 describes the moment the tint drains away.
screen: `A CLEAR BEAD ON RED CLOTH.` → `ON BLUE SILK. ON A LEAF.` → `NO COLOR OF ITS OWN.`

segments.voice: Sutra 1.41, in paraphrase: when the turnings have dwindled, the mind becomes like a fine, transparent jewel, and takes on the form of whatever it rests on, whether the knower, the act of knowing, or the thing known. That merging is called samapatti, coinciding. The crystal takes the color. Then Patanjali lays out the stages. First, savitarka, absorption on a coarse object, still mixed with three things: the word, the object, and the idea of it. Vyasa's example is a cow: the sound cow, the animal, and the thought of a cow, all tangled together. Next, nirvitarka. Memory is cleaned out, the mind becomes as if empty of its own form, and only the object shines. Not the label cow. Just the cow, seen. Sutra 1.44 says the same two steps happen with subtle objects: savichara, still with some thinking, and nirvichara, without it. Sutra 1.45 says subtle objects go all the way back to the unmanifest, the root of nature itself. And sutra 1.46 gathers the whole set: these are samadhi with seed. You met that phrase ten days ago. Now you know what the seeds are: every object, coarse or subtle, that the clear mind still rests on. Notice how practical the first step is. Most of the time we don't see things; we see their names. The crystal begins when the name drops away for a moment, and the thing itself is simply there.
screen: `THE MIND LIKE A TRANSPARENT JEWEL.` · `SAVITARKA: WORD, THING, IDEA.` · `NIRVITARKA: ONLY THE OBJECT SHINES.` · then, large: `ALL OF THESE: WITH SEED.`

segments.voice: Before you close your eyes, pick an object near you: a cup, a plant, your own hand. Look at it. Notice the name arrive: cup. Notice ideas follow: mine, chipped, needs washing. Now, gently, let the name and ideas go, and just look. Shape, light, color. If the label comes back, let it pass. Then close your eyes and keep the object in mind, without words, like the crystal on the cloth. The bell holds the time.
The stages of absorption. With thought and without, on coarse objects and on subtle ones: the steps of samadhi with seed, in sutras 1.41 to 1.46.
Your line: the crystal takes the color. Once today, look at something ordinary for ten seconds without naming it, and let it show you its own color. Day four hundred forty-four.

howItsDone: Teachers of classical yoga describe samapatti as the mind becoming transparent to its object, and they guide students from coarse objects, such as an image or the breath, toward subtler ones over long practice.

match.prompt: the stages, in order: tap the pairs.
pairs: the mind takes the object's form

myth: in sutra 1.41 the clear mind changes into the object
like a crystal, it takes the object's color without being changed itself.
Vyasa's example of word, object and idea is a cow
the sound cow, the animal, and the thought of it, mixed together in savitarka.
sutra 1.46 calls all these stages samadhi with seed
they all still rest on an object.

fork.setup: you're absorbed in a flower, but the word 'flower' and thoughts about it keep running. which stage is this?
options: savitarka: word, object and idea still mixed.
fork.reveal: savitarka: absorption on a coarse object, still mixed with word and idea. when the label falls away and only the flower shines, that's nirvitarka.

original.note: Sanskrit samāpatti: coinciding, the clear mind taking the form of its object, like a crystal taking a color.

trapdoor: what you thought: absorption means getting lost.
what it means: the mind gets so clear that the object shows through it perfectly, first with labels, then without.

what a scholar hears: 1.41–1.46 map samapatti on grahitri, grahana and grahya (knower, knowing, known) through savitarka, nirvitarka, savichara and nirvichara, up to the unmanifest (alinga); all sabija.
